rationale: Two commits on top of the merged Yana-review response chain: (1) b4e8b06f2 added mutual-exclusion between GitHub and GitLab provider fields via shouldShow predicates keyed on non-sensitive companion fields (github_event_filter / gitlab_event_filter) so editing an existing webhook with a blanked sensitive token still gates the other provider; also added a note on gitlab_event_filter clarifying that non-MR events pass through the filter, matching the backend contract fixed in codemie MR !3758 commit 03d96d935. (2) 63ee8d5b1 reverted the shouldShow gating after Ihor Nasukho proposed a section-based layout instead — a single webhook URL may legitimately receive events from multiple providers, so hiding one provider when the other is filled removes a valid workflow. Introduced CredentialComponentType.sectionHeader (pseudo-field that renders <h5> + divider inline, no Controller, no form value), interleaved five headers into the webhook fields config (General → Request verification (legacy header) → GitHub → GitLab → Target resource), and suppressed the outer 'Authentication' heading via fieldsSectionTitle:'' so section titles are not duplicated. Tests: replaced the mutual-exclusion suite with (a) config-shape assertions locking section order and provider-fields ungating, (b) a rendering test confirming each sectionHeader materializes as an <h5> and does not emit a form input. Standards: commit subjects match .ai-run/guides/standards/git-workflow.md format (EPMCDME-8384: <Description>). QA gates local: lint clean, tsc --noEmit clean, vitest CredentialFields.test.tsx 18/18 pass, gitleaks clean.

business_review.topic: UX layout aligns with reviewer request
business_review.notes: Section order and labels mirror the mockup Ihor Nasukho posted on MR !1522 (note 2292672); commit description explicitly references the reviewer's proposal.
gitlab_event_filter note text matches semantics implemented in codemie MR !3758 (non-MR events bypass filter; filtered MR actions ACK 200).

standards_review.notes: Both new commits use EPMCDME-8384: <capitalised description> as required.

standards_review.notes: Section headers are pure presentational pseudo-fields with no validation coupling; existing multiselect Yup validator remains the source of truth.
npm run lint and npm run typecheck both exit clean on the touched files (CredentialFields.tsx, MultiSelectCheckboxGroup test, settingsUIConfig.ts, settingsUI.ts).
Pure UI restructure; no auth, no secrets, no data-flow changes.
